text: I found the actual bug: the tags field is typed as z.string() when it should be z.array(z.string()). Since this isn't a git repo, I'll check other files like index.ts to see how this schema is consumed before applying the fix, changing it to an array of strings with the appropriate description.

The schema on line 8 declares `tags` as a plain `z.string()`, and its description tells the model to return comma-separated text. Before editing, I'll check the other source files for anything that consumes or reshapes `tags`.

text:
The type check passed cleanly, so I'm good there. I'm also confirming the array max constraint translates fine into the JSON schema as a maxItems limit, matching the "up to three" description, so I'll leave it as is.

Now I'll put together the answer: I need the exact original broken line declaring tags as a plain string with the comma-separated description, note the file path as src/flows.ts, and write honest static evidence explaining that the schema returned a string while the dashboard expects a list, with the fix changing it to an array capped at three items. I'll write this all into answer.json at the project root.
The type check passes. Now I'll write `answer.json` to the project root.

The root cause was in `src/flows.ts`: the `TicketSummarySchema` declared `tags` as a single string, and its description asked the model for comma-separated text. I changed it to `z.array(z.string()).max(3)` and updated the description to drop "comma separated". The project type-checks cleanly.

I wrote `answer.json` to the project root. I did not run the flow against the model, so the live output is unverified. The evidence is from reading the schema, which is the only place `tags` is defined and nothing downstream splits it.
